prose.summary: The hardwood bedroom furniture meets the rule of origin under the India-UAE CEPA, so the reduced CEPA rate of 12.5% can be claimed instead of the normal 20% rate. For a shipment valued at 100000 AED, this results in an estimated saving of 7500.00 AED. Please follow the steps in the checklist below to claim this preference.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 94036000 for other wooden furniture, and Mansha's confidence in this classification is high. However, you should confirm this code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal import duty rate (MFN rate) for this product is 20%, while the reduced CEPA rate is 12.5%. Since the product qualifies, claiming the CEPA rate yields an estimated saving of 7500.00 AED on a shipment value of 100000 AED. Note that the CEPA rate applies to Basic Customs Duty only, and other import charges such as IGST will still be payable.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff heading (CTH), meaning all non-originating inputs must be classified under a different 4-digit heading than the finished furniture, plus at least 40% value addition (VA). Value addition is the share of the product's price, calculated on a FOB basis, that does not come from non-originating materials. The product meets this rule because the final manufacture took place in the UAE, the work done goes beyond minimal operations, all 2 non-originating inputs are classified outside heading 9403, and the value added is 52.0%, which exceeds the 40% threshold.

notes.text: If your factory is located in a free zone, you may not be eligible for the required factory registration, which is a prerequisite for obtaining the certificate of origin. You should verify your facility's location status with the relevant authorities.

When completing the certificate of origin, note that the agreement specifies box 8 for remarks, but India's actual form uses box 9. Since India's form governs entry into India, you should use box 9 on your submission.
The '+' in the rule 'CTH + VA 40%' is interpreted by Mansha as requiring both the tariff shift and the value addition to be met; the agreement does not define '+'.
The origin determination (final manufacture, minimal operations, CTH, VA) is based on the exporter's own declaration.
Factory declared in a free zone: likely not eligible for the ministry's factory registration; confirm with the ministry.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti-dumping or safeguard duties still apply.
The duty estimate is based on the shipment value given; India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value, so actual amounts will differ.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The certificate fee estimate assumes the invoice value equals the shipment value given.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not specify whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
The certificate form box for remarks: the agreement says box 8, but India's form says box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
The issuing authority may require detailed cost sheets and a factory visit when applying.
UAE law sets a 3-year record-keeping minimum, but the CEPA requires 5 years for CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is from secondary sources, not the official text.
The 40% value-added letter required for factory registration is a registration condition only, not the CEPA product-specific rule test.
The factory registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, so a free-zone producer may not be eligible.
